analysis.title: Scene of the Crime: High-Beta Momentum's Reclaimed Thursday's Drop, But History Says Expect More Downside Ahead
key_insights: BTIG's Jonathan Krinsky treats high-beta momentum stocks as the dominant factor in the current market. He studied dates when the high-beta momentum index fell at least 10% in a day and then gained 5% or more in a day within the next three trading days.

Study result: 30-day forward returns were negative seven of eight times, averaging -10%. All eight events saw at least a -9% drawdown over the next 50 days, and seven saw at least a -16% drawdown. None of the events marked the final bottom of the correction or bear market.

The 'scene of the crime' pattern: price often returns to where the waterfall decline started last week. After that revisit, price tends to resume the direction of the impulsive move, which here would be down.
Overhead supply in SOXX: heavy volume traded above $165, so any purchase made from May through early November is now underwater. BTIG says that limits upside even if the rally extends.
BTIG would be wrong if SOXX trades firmly above $165, which would suggest the recent move was a 'false breakdown'. The SOXX 200-day moving average is about $160.
Short of that, BTIG treats rallies as counter-trend and as chances to reduce exposure ahead of a full move back toward the April breakout point of $115-$120.
CPI is due the day after the report (published November 9, 2026). BTIG notes NFP and CPI have been among the least discussed data events in recent memory given the market volatility.

Crude oil fell about 20% in a few days and the data center/AI trade broke, both helping inflation expectations. One-year swap spreads fell about 90bps in eight days, the largest such move in at least six years.
Some of the drop in inflation expectations comes from the fall in the data center/AI space, so BTIG cautions 'be careful what you wish for'.
BTIG expects a hot CPI to be looked through and a cool CPI to cause a knee-jerk move higher. It would treat any post-CPI pop as a chance to reduce risk, since the reaction to the reaction matters.

sector_views.rationale: Heavy overhead supply above $165 and a view that rallies are counter-trend, with a target of a full move back toward $115-$120.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Largest such move in at least six years. Part of the drop reflects the break in the data center/AI trade.
A hot print would likely be looked through, and a cool print would likely cause a knee-jerk move higher. BTIG would use any post-CPI pop to reduce risk.
macro_indicators.period: release due the day after November 9, 2026

trade_ideas.description: Reduce long exposure into rallies, including any post-CPI pop, in high-beta momentum and semiconductors (SOXX).
trade_ideas.rationale: Historical study shows negative 30-day forward returns after a similar sharp drop and rebound, and SOXX has heavy overhead supply above $165.
trade_ideas.risk: SOXX trading firmly above $165 would suggest a false breakdown.

risk_factors: SOXX trading firmly above $165 would show demand outweighing supply and suggest a false breakdown.
A cool CPI could cause a knee-jerk rally, which BTIG would use to reduce risk.
The fall in inflation expectations is partly tied to the AI/data center selloff, which carries its own risk.
vol_and_positioning: The high-beta momentum long index had a -10% or worse daily decline followed by a 5%+ daily gain within three days in eight historical events. Forward returns after those events were volatile with a negative skew.
SOXX volume distribution shows heavy volume above $165, so buyers from May through early November are underwater, creating overhead supply.

tension_points.bull_case: High-beta momentum reclaimed Thursday's drop, and if SOXX trades firmly above $165 the move could be a false breakdown with demand outweighing supply.
tension_points.bear_case: In eight similar historical events, 30-day forward returns were negative seven times, averaging -10%, and heavy overhead supply above $165 limits upside.
tension_points.what_invalidates: SOXX trading firmly above $165 would invalidate the bearish view.

theme_stances.evidence: none of them marked the ultimate bottom for the correction or bear market
